items.title: Agencies reduce regulatory burden for community banks, increase eligibility for 18-month exam cycle
items.summary: Agencies reduce regulatory burden for community banks, increase eligibility for 18-month exam cycle
items.why: Interagency regulatory rule change expanding exam cycle eligibility for community banks.

items.title: One Nation pushes for early super access for renters and mortgage holders
items.summary: Australians would be given the option to divert a portion of their superannuation into their take-home pay for up to three years.
items.why: New political proposal to allow temporary diversion of superannuation into take-home pay.

items.title: Government cites cost of living as reason to break its promise on recycling
items.summary: Industry groups say they were left blindsided by the federal government's decision to scrap mandatory standards for packaging.
items.why: Government policy reversal scrapping promised mandatory packaging standards.

items.title: Government to stop super being drained through fraud
items.summary: Perpetrators of domestic violence would be punished rather than rewarded for their actions when committing abuse against their former partners through the tax and super systems.
items.why: New government policy initiative targeting tax and superannuation system fraud in domestic abuse cases.

items.title: 'Battery cowboys' accused of gaming taxpayer-funded scheme
items.summary: Almost 100 whistleblower tip-offs claim dodgy operators are rorting a multi-billion-dollar taxpayer-funded solar battery program by mocking up installs, forging signatures and using unlicensed tradies for cash jobs.
items.why: Major whistleblower allegations regarding fraud in a multi-billion-dollar taxpayer-funded subsidy scheme.

items.title: Israel closes UK consulate in East Jerusalem as three G7 countries ban settlement imports
items.summary: Britain, France and Canada will ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, in a move that prompted a swift retaliation and could spark a broader geopolitical storm.
items.why: Britain, France, and Canada implement new import bans on West Bank settlement goods.

items.title: Small businesses fighting to stay open amid 'insidious cost creep'
items.summary: Small business owners hit with rising costs will no longer be able to add surcharges on card payments from October 1. One operator in regional South Australia has described it as an "insidious cost creep".
items.why: New ban prohibiting small businesses from adding card payment surcharges starting October 1 alters payments policy.

items.title: 'Perfect storm': How banks allegedly defrauded of up to $600m
items.summary: NSW police say one of Australia's largest fraud syndicates has fleeced banks of up to $600 million in fraudulent loans in what one investigator described as the largest financial crime he has seen.
items.why: Major police action uncovering an alleged $600 million bank loan fraud syndicate.

items.title: Why these big new AI data centres are set to escape new regulations
items.summary: Dozens of approved but yet-to-be-built AI data centre projects will escape the federal government's proposed restrictions around energy and water use because the new rules are not expected to be retrospective.
items.why: New proposed energy and water restrictions for data centres will not apply retrospectively to already approved projects.

items.title: Being a renter, Jenny missed out on solar boon but that is about to change
items.summary: Australia readies to lift a ban on plug-in solar, unlocking access to the technology for millions of apartment dwellers and renters for the first time.
items.why: Lifting a regulatory ban on plug-in solar represents a significant policy change opening access for renters.
